title: 699. The Troubles: Return of the IRA (Part 3)

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 您好。

sentences.en: Now, before we go to today's episode, I have some insanely exciting news for you.
sentences.zh: 好，在进入今天的节目之前，我有个让人兴奋到疯狂的消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: On Friday, the 4th of September, Dominic and I will be forming live at the South Bank Centre in London.
sentences.zh: 9月4日（星期五），多米尼克和我将在伦敦的南岸中心进行现场演出。

sentences.en: And better yet, we will be doing something completely new, something that no one has ever heard before on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 更棒的是，我们将做一些完全不同的尝试，这是在《历史的余烬》中从未听到过的内容。

sentences.en: The ultimate Victorian adventure.
sentences.zh: 终极的维多利亚时期大冒险。

sentences.en: So to give you just a little taste, we will be in Africa in 1868.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家先睹为快，我们将回到1868年的非洲。

sentences.en: The Emperor of Abyssinia, Theodore II, has kidnapped 59 Europeans and he is holding them hostage after descending into this demented rage
sentences.zh: 阿比西尼亚皇帝特沃德罗斯二世在陷入疯狂的暴怒后，绑架了59名欧洲人并将他们作为人质，

sentences.en: because one of his fellow monarchs, Queen Victoria, has declined to answer his letters.
sentences.zh: 因为他的同行君主维多利亚女王拒绝回信给他。

sentences.en: I'm not making this up.
sentences.zh: 我可不是在瞎编。

sentences.en: And the British, after months and months of fruitless waiting, have lost patience
sentences.zh: 英国人在经历了几个月毫无结果的等待后，已经失去了耐心，

sentences.en: and they have sent a military expedition under General Napier halfway around the world to save them.
sentences.zh: 他们派遣了由内皮尔将军率领的军事远征军远渡重洋去营救这些人。

sentences.en: An expedition that includes thousands of mules, loads of elephants,
sentences.zh: 这支远征军包括数千头骡子、成群的大象，

sentences.en: and they've even had to build their own railway across the highlands of Abyssinia or Ethiopia to try to get to his mountain citadel.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不得不在阿比西尼亚或埃塞俄比亚的高原上修建自己的铁路，试图到达他的山间堡垒。

sentences.en: Well, it is a bonkers story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真是一个疯狂的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's absolutely extraordinary, full-blown British imperial epic full of ludicrous behaviour,
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对是一场非同寻常、原汁原味的英国帝国史诗，充满了荒谬的行为、

sentences.en: mad characters, colossal moustaches, everything that we love on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的人物、巨大的胡须，这些都是我们在《历史的余烬》中最喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: It is, though I say so myself, a guaranteed classic in the making.
sentences.zh: 虽说由我来评价有点自吹自擂，但这绝对是一部注定流传后世的经典。

sentences.en: So you're probably thinking, how can I get a ticket for this extraordinary Victorian adventure?
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会想，我该如何买到这张参加非凡维多利亚大冒险的门票呢？

sentences.en: Here is the answer.
sentences.zh: 答案就在这里。

sentences.en: If you want to get a ticket for this event on Friday, the 4th of September, all you have to do is to go to TheRestIsHistory.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你想买到9月4日星期五这场活动的门票，你只需要访问 TheRestIsHistory.com。

sentences.en: It is as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就是这么简单。

sentences.en: You maybe have to part with some money, but it will be money very, very, very, very well spent.
sentences.zh: 你可能得花掉一些钱，但这笔钱绝对、绝对、绝对、绝对花得太值了。

sentences.en: See you there.
sentences.zh: 到时见。

sentences.en: Down through the centuries, the people of Ireland have been forced to wage a continuing and arduous struggle for freedom and equality.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，爱尔兰人民被迫为争取自由和平等展开了持续而艰苦的斗争。

sentences.en: For generations, division and despair have scarred the countryside.
sentences.zh: 几代人以来，分裂和绝望在乡间留下了斑斑伤痕。

sentences.en: Often alone, often without notice from others throughout the world, brave men and women of Ireland have given their lives for the principles they hold dear.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰勇敢的男男女女常常孤军奋战，常常不为世人所瞩目，却为他们珍视的原则献出了生命。

sentences.en: Today, the Irish struggle again.
sentences.zh: 今天，爱尔兰再次陷入斗争。

sentences.en: The crisis now, however, is especially serious, because the hate and bitterness are taking a new and far more drastic turn.
sentences.zh: 然而，当前的危机尤为严重，因为仇恨和痛苦正在发生一种全新且更为激烈的转变。

sentences.en: Ulster teeters on the brink of a civil war that threatens to engulf all of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 阿尔斯特正处于内战的边缘，这场内战有可能吞没整个爱尔兰。

sentences.en: The government of Ulster rules by bayonet and bloodshed.
sentences.zh: 阿尔斯特政府靠刺刀和流血进行统治。

sentences.en: The soaring toll of death and violence is uncontrolled.
sentences.zh: 死亡和暴力的伤亡人数飙升，失控蔓延。

sentences.en: Thousands flee their homes in terror.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人惊恐地逃离家园。

sentences.en: Businesses are bombed and factories close down.
sentences.zh: 企业遭到炸弹袭击，工厂纷纷倒闭。

sentences.en: Barbed wire roadblocks imprison every street corner.
sentences.zh: 铁丝网路障封锁了每一个街角。

sentences.en: Young children stand on curbstones and shout shrill insults filled with hate.
sentences.zh: 幼儿站在路边，尖叫着充满仇恨的侮辱性言语。

sentences.en: Ulster is becoming.
sentences.zh: 阿尔斯特正在变成

sentences.en: Britain's.
sentences.zh: 英国的

sentences.en: Britain's.
sentences.zh: 英国的。

sentences.en: So that was Senator Edward Kennedy taking time off from driving young women into tidal ponds
sentences.zh: 以上是参议员爱德华·肯尼迪在1971年10月20日抽空发表的讲话，他当时刚把年轻女性开进潮汐池里，

sentences.en: and then pretending it never happened to make a helpful intervention on the plight of Northern Ireland in the United States Congress on the 20th of October 1971.
sentences.zh: 然后装作什么都没发生的样子，在美国国会就北爱尔兰的困境进行了适时的干预。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, this was a speech that went down in Britain like a cup of cold sick.
sentences.zh: 而且，多米尼克，这场演讲在英国引起的恶劣反响就像是一杯冷呕吐物。

sentences.en: And I suppose the members of the British population who particularly enjoyed it were the Protestant majority in Northern Ireland itself.
sentences.zh: 我想，英国人口中特别喜欢这一幕的应该是北爱尔兰本土的抗议宗多数派。

sentences.en: But having said that, it did go down very well with Catholics in Northern Ireland, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，它在北爱尔兰的天主教徒中确实反响很好，不是吗？

sentences.en: And indeed in Ireland more generally.
sentences.zh: 在整个爱尔兰也确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对如此。

sentences.en: So, hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 那么，大家好。

sentences.en: That was a remarkable attempt on Ted Kennedy's voice there.
sentences.zh: 那是对泰德·肯尼迪声音的一次非凡模仿。

sentences.en: I thought, ironically, given their antagonism...
sentences.zh: 我想，考虑到他们的对立，讽刺的是……

sentences.en: It actually sounded more like Jimmy Carter.
sentences.zh: 听起来其实更像吉米·卡特。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 对，我知道。

sentences.en: I finally got there after months of practice.
sentences.zh: 经过几个月的练习，我终于模仿到位了。

sentences.en: I was trying to make it nasal and for some reason it went Southern.
sentences.zh: 我本想让它带点鼻音，但不知为何听起来成了美国南部口音。

sentences.en: It's great to have Jimmy Carter back on the show, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 吉米·卡特重返节目真是太棒了，对吧？

sentences.en: Anyway, so this speech, yeah, kicked off an absolute firestorm of controversy.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，所以这段演讲，是的，引发了一场绝对的争议风暴。

sentences.en: So the British Embassy in Washington issued a kind of rare statement of rebuke.
sentences.zh: 因此，英国驻华盛顿大使馆罕见地发表了一份谴责声明。

sentences.en: It said, our troops in Northern Ireland are there to stop murder and bloodshed.
sentences.zh: 声明称，我们在北爱尔兰的军队是为了制止谋杀和流血事件。

sentences.en: And actually, if a majority of people in Northern Ireland want to join the Republic of Ireland, we will not stand in their way.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果北爱尔兰的大多数人想要加入爱尔兰共和国，我们不会阻拦。

sentences.en: We're not holding them by bayonets and bullets and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们没有用刺刀和子弹扣留他们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Kennedy's intervention is a sign, I think, of just how toxic Northern Ireland had become for Britain, for the image of Great Britain in the early 1970s.
sentences.zh: 我认为肯尼迪的干预表明，在20世纪70年代初，北爱尔兰问题对英国以及大英帝国的形象而言已经变得多么具有毒性。

sentences.en: And his comparison with Vietnam, which was incredibly controversial in late 1971, given what was happening in Vietnam, was it accurate?
sentences.zh: 考虑到当时越南正在发生的事情，他在1971年底将北爱尔兰与越南进行对比——这在当时极具争议——这种对比准确吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's not that far-fetched.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这并非完全牵强附会。

sentences.en: So at this point, at the end of 1971, about 200 people have been killed.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1971年底这个时候，大约有200人丧生。

sentences.en: Of course, nothing by the numbers being killed in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与越南的死亡人数相比微不足道。

sentences.en: But the spectacle of an army trapped in a quagmire, you know, where it's hard to tell friend from foe, where there's no political solution in sight.
sentences.zh: 但军队陷入泥潭的景象，你知道，在那里很难分清敌友，看不到政治解决方案的曙光。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a lack of napalm, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就是缺少了凝固汽油弹，对吧？

sentences.en: There is a lack of napalm, but there is the sense of a conflict spiralling out of control and politicians haplessly struggling to keep up.
sentences.zh: 确实缺少凝固汽油弹，但确实有一种冲突失控、政客们无助挣扎着难以跟上的感觉。

sentences.en: I mean, there are definite, you know, dissimilarities, no question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，两者之间确实有明显的不同之处，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: But rather as the Americans, when they first went into Vietnam, thought, well, this will be done and dusted quite quickly and we'll be able to go home.
sentences.zh: 但正如美国人刚进入越南时以为，这很快就会平息，我们就能回家一样。

sentences.en: Similarly, when the British sent in the army, as we heard last time, in the late summer of 1969,
sentences.zh: 同样，正如我们上次听到的那样，当英国人在1969年夏末派遣军队时，

sentences.en: and of course they sent troops to protect, largely to protect the Catholic populations of Belfast and London Derry,
sentences.zh: 当然，他们派遣军队是为了保护，主要是为了保护贝尔法斯特和伦敦德里的天主教徒人口，

sentences.en: they thought, well, hopefully we'll be home, not by Christmas, but within a few months.
sentences.zh: 他们当时想，好吧，希望我们能回家，不是在圣诞节前，而是在几个月内。

sentences.en: And the story of today's episode is how all of that went wrong.
sentences.zh: 今天这一集的故事讲的就是这一切是如何走向错误方向的。

sentences.en: How did things become so bitter and so murderous so quickly in a way that would lead outside observers to make a comparison with what was going on in Vietnam?
sentences.zh: 为什么事情会以这样一种方式迅速变得如此痛苦和充满谋杀意味，以至于让局外观察家将之与越南正在发生的事情进行比较？

sentences.en: So let's kick off by reminding ourselves where we got to last time.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们先回顾一下上期节目我们讲到了哪里。

sentences.en: So we had Northern Ireland, established in the 1920s, with this deep sort of fracture line,
sentences.zh: 因此，20世纪20年代建立的北爱尔兰有着这样一条深深的分裂线，

sentences.en: Protestant majority, Catholic minority, the Catholic minority feeling they're treated like second-class citizens and everything from jobs to housing.
sentences.zh: 新教徒多数派，天主教徒少数派，天主教少数派觉得他们在从工作到住房的方方面面都被当作二等公民对待。

sentences.en: In the first episode last week, we talked about how things started to spiral downhill in the mid-1960s,
sentences.zh: 在上周的第一集中，我们讨论了事情是如何在20世纪60年代中期开始走下坡路的，

sentences.en: Terence O'Neill's attempts to modernise,
sentences.zh: 特伦斯·奥尼尔的现代化尝试，

sentences.en: Ian Paisley's inflammatory kind of rhetoric, the anniversary of the Easter Rising, the first killings by the Ulster Volunteer Force in 1966.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·佩斯利的煽动性言论，复活节起义纪念日，阿尔斯特志愿军在1966年的首次杀戮。

sentences.en: And then last episode, the emergence of the Catholic Civil Rights Movement,
sentences.zh: 然后是上一集，天主教民权运动的兴起，

sentences.en: this sort of increasing sense of confrontation, the Battle of the Bogside, as it was called in Derry, and Wilson and Callaghan agreeing to send in the troops.
sentences.zh: 这种日益增强的对抗感，德里的博格赛德之战，以及威尔逊和卡拉汉同意派遣军队。

sentences.en: So let's pick up the story in the mid-summer of 1970, and specifically we're on the 21st of June.
sentences.zh: 让我们从1970年仲夏开始继续讲这个故事，具体来说是6月21日。

sentences.en: Now, Harold Wilson, with his shiny Ganex raincoat, is out.
sentences.zh: 现在，穿着闪亮加内克斯雨衣的哈罗德·威尔逊已经出局了。

sentences.en: He's gone.
sentences.zh: 他已经走了。

sentences.en: He's gone from the story.
sentences.zh: 他退出了故事。

sentences.en: He has lost the election.
sentences.zh: 他输掉了大选。

sentences.en: He lost it three days earlier on the 18th of June.
sentences.zh: 他在三天前的6月18日输掉了大选。

sentences.en: And so, Tom, we welcome back to the show a great yachtsman, a great organ scholar, but a man who hates a traditional county, and that man is Ted Heath.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我们欢迎一位伟大的游艇手、一位伟大的管风琴学者、但又是一个痛恨传统郡的人重返节目，这个人就是泰德·希思。

sentences.en: The worst man in history, apart from Jimmy Carter.
sentences.zh: 历史上最糟糕的人，除了吉米·卡特。

sentences.en: You think Ted Heath is the worst man than Jimmy Carter?
sentences.zh: 你认为泰德·希思比吉米·卡特还要糟糕吗？

sentences.en: What he did to Rutland is unforgivable.
sentences.zh: 他对拉特兰郡做的事是不可原谅的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the ridings.
sentences.zh: 还有那些行政区划分。

sentences.en: Mad counties.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的郡。

sentences.en: Mad counties.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的郡。

sentences.en: And Heath is personally to blame.
sentences.zh: 而且希思本人难辞其咎。

sentences.en: I think that's the takeaway from this series.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是本系列要得出的结论。

sentences.en: So Heath, the leader of the Conservative Party, has just won the general election.
sentences.zh: 因此，保守党领袖希思刚刚赢得了大选。

sentences.en: He hasn't talked at all about Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他根本没有谈论北爱尔兰。

sentences.en: He's talked about overhauling the British economy to get rid of all the lame ducks in industry.
sentences.zh: 他一直在谈论彻底改革英国经济，以清除工业中所有的跛脚鸭。

sentences.en: But, I mean, he's a conscious moderniser, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，他是一个有意识的现代化主义者，不是吗？

sentences.en: So he would have no interest in Northern Ireland, which he would see as a kind of antediluvian 17th century Borg.
sentences.zh: 所以他对北爱尔兰不会有任何兴趣，在他看来，北爱尔兰是一个远古时代的17世纪堡垒。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: And, of course, he wants to be friendly to Britain's neighbours because he wants to get us into the common market.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，他希望对英国的邻居们友好，因为他想让我们加入共同市场。

sentences.en: So Britain will join along with Ireland in 1973.
sentences.zh: 所以英国将在1973年与爱尔兰一同加入。

sentences.en: Ted Heath, it would astound you to hear, given what we were saying about Britain's politicians in the last episodes, has absolutely no knowledge of Northern Ireland
sentences.zh: 考虑到我们在前几集中对英国政客的评价，泰德·希思对北爱尔兰毫无了解，这一定会让你大吃一惊。

sentences.en: and no interest in it whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 并且对它毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: So on the 21st of June, which is where we're kicking off, the Cabinet Secretary has the excellent name of Sir Burke Trend.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们开始讲述的6月21日，内阁秘书有一个非常棒的名字叫伯克·特伦德爵士。

sentences.en: Sir Burke Trend.
sentences.zh: 伯克·特伦德爵士。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's his name.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是他的名字。

sentences.en: That's an insane name.
sentences.zh: 这名字太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Well, that's his name.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是他的名字。

sentences.en: American-style name.
sentences.zh: 美式风格的名字。

sentences.en: I'm never going to be rude about an American name again.
sentences.zh: 我再也不会对美国名字无礼了。

sentences.en: So Sir Burke Trend sends him this briefing document and says, okay, this is the situation.
sentences.zh: 于是伯克·特伦德爵士向他发送了一份简报文件，并说，好吧，这就是现在的局势。

sentences.en: You know, I'm going to tell you everything you need to know about Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我要告诉你关于北爱尔兰你需要知道的一切。

sentences.en: And Sir Burke says to him, it's now 10 months since we're sent in the army and we hope to bring them home quickly, but obviously that ship has sailed.
sentences.zh: 伯克爵士对他说，我们派军队过去已经10个月了，我们曾希望迅速把他们带回家，但显然时过境迁，那个时机已经错过了。

sentences.en: And he says there are basically two scenarios.
sentences.zh: 他说基本上有两种情况。

sentences.en: The best case scenario is that things stay exactly as they are, and I quote, stabilised by the presence of British troops and trembling on the edge of disaster,
sentences.zh: 最好的情况是事情保持原样，引述他的话，“由英国军队的存在维持稳定，在灾难的边缘瑟瑟发抖”，

sentences.en: but never quite tipping over.
sentences.zh: 但从未真正倾覆。

sentences.en: And Burke Trend says, the downside is that it's going to be very expensive in terms of men and money.
sentences.zh: 伯克·特伦德说，不利的一面是，这将在人员和金钱方面付出高昂的代价。

sentences.en: However, that's the rosy scenario.
sentences.zh: 然而，这还算是乐观的情况。

sentences.en: The worst possibility as follows.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的可能性如下。

sentences.en: It could get worse and finally tip over the edge.
sentences.zh: 情况可能会恶化，最终彻底倾覆。

sentences.en: The Northern Ireland government proving incapable of holding the position, civil war breaking out within the province and Dublin being compelled to intervene.
sentences.zh: 北爱尔兰政府证明无力维持阵地，省内爆发内战，都柏林被迫干涉。

sentences.en: This would present us with a political and constitutional crisis of the first order.
sentences.zh: 这将给我们带来一级政治和宪法危机。

sentences.en: I mean, Dominic, you compared it, well, Edward Kennedy did, to Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多米尼克，你把它比作——嗯，爱德华·肯尼迪把它比作——越南。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But actually what it sounds like is Iraq or Afghanistan,
sentences.zh: 但实际上这听起来很像伊拉克或阿富汗，

sentences.en: the briefings that American presidents were probably getting
sentences.zh: 也就是美国总统们可能收到的简报，

sentences.en: in the wake of the attempt to stabilise those governments.

sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我们将看到的，有人试图基本上进行某种大卫·彼得雷乌斯式的增兵。

sentences.en: You know, in this similar kind of debates, do we get out?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在类似这种争论中，我们要撤军吗？

sentences.zh: 我们要投入更多军队吗？

sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做？

sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们要像那样把好钱扔进水里去追讨坏钱吗？

sentences.zh: 这个比喻一点也不坏。

sentences.en: So that's the picture.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前的画面。

sentences.en: But what Sir Bert, Trent and Ted Heath do not know is that at this point, a new factor is about to enter the equation.
sentences.zh: 但伯特·特伦特爵士和泰德·希思不知道的是，此时此刻，一个新的变数即将进入这个方程。

sentences.en: Now, one group that we actually haven't talked about that much, which may surprise some listeners, is the Irish Republican Army, the IRA.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一个我们实际上没有怎么谈论过的群体，这可能会让一些听众感到惊讶，那就是爱尔兰共和军，简称爱解军。

sentences.en: And the reason that, as we've talked about before, they had this border campaign that failed by 1962.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前讨论过的，原因在于他们曾有过一场到1962年宣告失败的边境运动。

sentences.en: The leadership of the IRA abandoned guerrilla violence.
sentences.zh: 爱解军的领导层放弃了游击暴力。

sentences.en: They put on their polo necks and they turned to kind of Marxism and hanging around with academics.
sentences.zh: 他们穿上高领毛衣，转向了某种马克思主义，并开始和学者们混在一起。

sentences.en: And they thought about, you know, they thought that the future of this movement is a workers' alliance to beat capitalism as well as imperialism.
sentences.zh: 他们开始思考，你知道的，他们认为这个运动的未来是建立一个工人联盟，既击败资本主义也击败帝国主义。

sentences.en: And that meant that during all the disturbances in 1969 that we talked about last time, the IRA are actually quite quiet.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在我们在上集讨论过的1969年的所有骚乱期间，爱解军实际上相当安静。

sentences.en: And graffiti went up in Belfast that summer.
sentences.zh: 那年夏天贝尔法斯特出现了涂鸦：

sentences.en: IRA equals I ran away.
sentences.zh: “爱解军等于我逃跑了。”

sentences.en: Now, if you're an older IRA man, if you've been active in that guerrilla movement since, let's say, the 1940s, even longer, you are very embarrassed by this.
sentences.zh: 听着，如果你是一个老派的爱尔兰共和军成员，如果你从比如20世纪40年代甚至更早起就活跃在这个游击运动中，你对此会感到非常尴尬。

sentences.en: In fact, you're positively furious.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你简直怒不可遏。

sentences.en: So these older IRA veterans, often they're kind of cultural conservatives, very strongly Catholic.
sentences.zh: 所以这些年长的爱尔兰共和军老兵，他们通常带有某种文化保守主义色彩，信仰非常虔诚的天主教。

sentences.en: They don't have any truck with the Marxism and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不理会什么马克思主义那一套。

sentences.en: They're really fed up with this.
sentences.zh: 他们对此真的厌烦透顶。

sentences.en: They're like, why are we not getting stuck in?
sentences.zh: 他们的态度是，为什么我们还不直接大干一场？

sentences.en: And then the other group who I think are really important are the younger militants, often in their, you know, late teens, early 20s,
sentences.zh: 然后我认为另一个非常重要的群体是年轻的武装分子，他们通常，你知道的，处于十几岁到二十出头的年纪，

sentences.en: people who've seen action in the street fighting in Belfast and Derry in 1969.
sentences.zh: 也就是在1969年贝尔法斯特和德里的街头冲突中亲历过战斗的人。

sentences.en: And they similarly think the IRA has basically vacated its historic role as the defender of the Catholic people of Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他们同样认为，爱尔兰共和军基本上已经放弃了其作为北爱尔兰天主教人民捍卫者的历史使命。

sentences.en: You know, someone should take up arms to defend our people against the loyalists and the RUC and all of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，应该有人拿起武器来保护我们的人民免受保皇派、皇家阿尔斯特警察部队以及所有这些势力的侵害。

sentences.en: And this comes to a head in December 1969.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在1969年12月达到了白热化。

sentences.en: There's a secret meeting of disaffected IRA men in BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 贝尔法斯特举行了一次不满现状的爱尔兰共和军成员的秘密会议。

sentences.en: And they agree that they will split from the Marxist leadership and they will set up their own rival
sentences.zh: 他们一致同意脱离马克思主义领导层，并建立他们自己对立的

sentences.en: IRA executive and army council, as they're called.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰共和军执行委员会和军队委员会（正如他们所称的那样）。

sentences.en: And they call themselves the provisional IRA, partly to echo the text of the proclamation in the Easter Rising of 1916, which had set up a provisional government of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他们自称为“临时派爱尔兰共和军”，部分是为了呼应1916年复活节起义宣言的文本，当时该宣言曾建立了一个爱尔兰临时政府。

sentences.en: And what happens to the original IRA?
sentences.zh: 那么原本的爱尔兰共和军怎么样了？

sentences.en: Well, they still hang around.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们依然存在。

sentences.en: They have the official IRA.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为正式派爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: And are they still a going concern today?
sentences.zh: 那他们今天还在运营吗？

sentences.en: They effectively wound up their operations in the early 1970s, but they are still active in the period of this series.
sentences.zh: 他们在20世纪70年代初实际上结束了行动，但在本系列所讲述的时期内他们仍然很活跃。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they have gunmen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有枪手。

sentences.en: They have, you know, they have weapons.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们有武器。

sentences.en: They have seminars.
sentences.zh: 他们还有研讨会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, they become radicalised to try and compete with the provisionals, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了同临时派竞争，他们实际上变得激进化了。

sentences.en: So they sort of take up the gun as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他们某种程度上也拿起了枪。

sentences.en: But they end up merging, do they, basically?
sentences.zh: 但他们最后合并了吗，基本上？

sentences.en: No, they don't merge.
sentences.zh: 不，他们没有合并。

sentences.en: I mean, there's also the INLA, which we don't need to get into them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，还有爱尔兰国家解放军，我们不需要深入讨论他们。

sentences.en: You know, this is the nature of paramilitary groups.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是准军事组织的本质。

sentences.en: They tend to splinter.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会分裂。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So 10 days after this, so the provisional IRA issued their first public statements and they said, we're going to defend our people in the north.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这之后10天，临时派爱尔兰共和军发表了他们的第一份公开声明，他们说，我们要保卫我们在北方的同胞。

sentences.en: We're going to fight for the full political freedom of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 我们要为爱尔兰的完全政治自由而战。

sentences.en: And then early January 1970, the political wing of the IRA, so it had always had this allied political party called Sinn Féin, that split into official and provisional factions
sentences.zh: 接着在1970年1月上旬，爱尔兰共和军的政治翼——它一直有一个名为新芬党的附属政党——分裂成了官方派和临时派两个派别，

sentences.en: on the same lines.
sentences.zh: 沿着同样的路线分裂了。

sentences.en: And of course, it's the, as anyone, you know, who remembers the 1970s natives will know, it is the provisional IRA, the provos, that they are the people who dominate the headlines
sentences.zh: 当然，正如任何，你知道的，经历过20世纪70年代的当地人所知道的那样，正是临时派爱尔兰共和军（即“普罗沃斯”），在未来大约30年里，

sentences.en: in Britain and in Ireland in the next 30 years or so.
sentences.zh: 在英国和爱尔兰占据了各大媒体头条的正是他们。

sentences.en: So just to talk about them, because they are the group that everyone knows as the IRA.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来谈谈他们，因为他们就是每个人所熟知的那个爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: A couple of really important points.
sentences.zh: 有几个非常关键的要点。

sentences.en: Sometimes when you're reading about them, you will see people say, well, they were basically set up as a defensive organisation.
sentences.zh: 有时当你阅读关于他们的资料时，你会看到有人说，好吧，他们基本上是一个作为防御性组织建立起来的。

sentences.en: They were set up to defend
sentences.zh: 他们建立的目的是在1969年保护

sentences.en: Catholic communities from attacks by Protestant mobs in 1969, and that's where the provisionals came from.
sentences.zh: 天主教社区免受新教暴徒的袭击，临时派就是这样诞生的。

sentences.en: This is really just not true at all.
sentences.zh: 这完全不是事实。

sentences.en: So almost all of the original leaders of the provisionals, we'll talk about them a bit later, but a guy called
sentences.zh: 因此，临时派的几乎所有原始领导人——我们稍后会详细谈到他们——但有一个叫

sentences.zh: 肖恩·麦克史蒂芬的人，

sentences.en: Ruria Brady,
sentences.zh: 鲁里·布雷迪，

sentences.en: Davey O'Connell,
sentences.zh: 戴维·奥康奈尔，

sentences.en: Billy McKee.
sentences.zh: 比利·麦基。

sentences.en: These are long-standing
sentences.zh: 这些都是资深的

sentences.en: IRA men.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰共和军成员。

sentences.en: These are people who have been in the IRA for 10,
sentences.zh: 这些人加入爱尔兰共和军已经有10年、

sentences.en: 30 years.
sentences.zh: 30年了。

sentences.en: A lot of them have served time in prison in Britain or in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他们当中许多人曾在英国或爱尔兰的监狱里服刑。

sentences.en: These are paramilitaries who are, you know, they believe in using force to get a united Ireland.
sentences.zh: 这些准军事人员，你知道的，他们坚信使用武力来实现爱尔兰统一。

sentences.en: Now, even younger people associated with the IRA come from long-standing
sentences.zh: 如今，甚至与爱尔兰共和军相关联的年轻人也来自历史悠久的

sentences.en: Republican families.
sentences.zh: 共和派家庭。

sentences.en: Let's look at one person who very, very vigorously denies that he was ever part of the IRA.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看一个非常、非常坚决否认自己曾加入过爱尔兰共和军的人。

sentences.en: Can you guess who this person is?
sentences.zh: 你能猜出这个人是谁吗？

sentences.en: Is this Jerry Adams by any chance?
sentences.zh: 难道碰巧是杰里·亚当斯吗？

sentences.en: It is Jerry Adams, yes.
sentences.zh: 正是杰里·亚当斯，没错。

sentences.en: So we're just putting on the record that he does deny he was in the IRA.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要明确记录在案的是，他的确否认自己曾加入爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: He absolutely denies he was in the IRA.
sentences.zh: 他绝对否认自己曾加入爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: The strange thing about Jerry Adams is Jerry Adams denies that he was in the IRA, but every single academic historian who writes about this believes that he was.
sentences.zh: 关于杰里·亚当斯最奇怪的事情在于，他否认自己曾在爱尔兰共和军，但所有撰写相关历史的学术历史学家都认为他确实加入过。

sentences.en: So it's hard to know who to believe there,
sentences.zh: 所以很难知道该相信谁，

sentences.en: Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆。

sentences.en: So Jerry Adams was 21 years old when the provisionals were established.
sentences.zh: 因此，临时派成立时，杰里·亚当斯21岁。

sentences.en: Jerry Adams himself has always said, I was drawn into
sentences.zh: 杰里·亚当斯本人一直表示，我是通过民权运动被吸引进

sentences.en: Republican activism through the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 共和主义激进活动中的。

sentences.en: I was radicalized to join Sinn Féin because I was so shocked by the loyalist violence.
sentences.zh: 我之所以变得激进而加入新芬党，是因为我被保皇派的暴力行径深深震惊了。

sentences.en: That's important, isn't it, for the framing of the message for American audiences?
sentences.zh: 这对于向美国观众传递信息的包装来说很重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because if you cast yourself as being on the side of the civil rights movement, I mean, who would object to that?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你把自己塑造成站在民权运动这一边的人，我的意思是，谁会反对这个呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, who would disagree with that?
sentences.zh: 是的，谁会不同意这一点呢？

sentences.en: Now, it's important to say what Jerry Adams is saying here about being radicalized this way is just not true.
sentences.zh: 现在，必须要指出的是，杰里·亚当斯在这里关于自己因这种方式而激进化的说法完全不是真的。

sentences.en: Jerry Adams comes from a Republican family in West BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 杰里·亚当斯来自西贝尔法斯特的一个共和派家庭。

sentences.en: His grandfather was a member of the Irish
sentences.zh: 他的祖父是20世纪20年代爱尔兰

sentences.en: Republican Brotherhood in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 共和兄弟会的成员。

sentences.en: His father was in the IRA.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲曾加入爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: His uncles were in the IRA.
sentences.zh: 他的叔伯们也加入过爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: His father was jailed for an ambush on a police patrol.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲曾因伏击警察巡逻队而入狱。

sentences.en: So let's assume that Jerry Adams is telling the truth that he was never part of the IRA.
sentences.zh: 因此，假设杰里·亚当斯说的是真的，即他从未加入过爱尔兰共和军。

sentences.en: The puzzle for me is why he wasn't.
sentences.zh: 令我感到费解的是他为什么没有加入。

sentences.en: Because given his background, it would be very strange for him not to have joined it, I would say.
sentences.zh: 因为鉴于他的背景，我想说，他如果没有加入才真的很奇怪。

sentences.en: However, you know, it's a funny old world, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道的，这世界真是无奇不有，对吧？

sentences.en: So maybe he wasn't.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他真的没加入吧。

sentences.en: Now, the other point is about violence.
sentences.zh: 现在，另一个重点是关于暴力。

sentences.en: The provisional IRA, unlike the, say, the civil rights movement, are not interested in reforming the Stormont state.
sentences.zh: 临时派爱尔兰共和军，与民权运动等不同，他们对改革斯托蒙特政权毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: No, they want to destroy it, don't they?
sentences.zh: 没错，他们想要摧毁它，不是吗？

sentences.en: They want to destroy it.
sentences.zh: 他们想要摧毁它。

sentences.en: They want to bring down
sentences.zh: 他们想要推翻

sentences.en: Stormont, they want to drive out the British, and they want a united Ireland.
sentences.zh: 斯托蒙特，他们想要驱逐英国人，他们想要一个统一的爱尔兰。

sentences.en: And the way that they're going to do that is what they call euphemistically physical force.
sentences.zh: 而他们实现这一目标的方式就是他们委婉称之为的武力。

sentences.en: And that is violence.
sentences.zh: 也就是暴力。

sentences.en: And they're completely upfront about that.
sentences.zh: 他们对此直言不讳，毫无掩饰。

sentences.en: So this is the Republican
sentences.zh: 所以这是1970年9月的《共和报》

sentences.en: News in September 1970.
sentences.zh: 上的一段话。

sentences.en: It says, the Irish people should realise that British imperialists do not respect, fear, or pay much attention to people who beg, grovel, or crawl for favours or concessions.
sentences.zh: 它说，爱尔兰人民应该认识到，英国帝国主义者既不尊重、不畏惧，也不会过多关注那些为了施舍或妥协而乞求、卑躬屈膝或匍匐爬行的人。

sentences.en: In other words, they only respect you if you fight back.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，只有当你进行反击时，他们才会尊重你。

sentences.en: Now, of course, the IRA say, and they say this throughout,
sentences.zh: 当然，爱尔兰共和军会说，而且他们自始至终都在说，

sentences.en: there are going to be civilian casualties.
sentences.zh: 这必然会出现平民伤亡。

sentences.en: But this is a war.
sentences.zh: 但这是一场战争。

sentences.en: That is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: It is worth it.
sentences.zh: 这是值得的。

sentences.en: You know, we're going to be doing terrible things, but it is worth it to get what we want, and the end will justify the means.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们会做一些可怕的事情，但为了得到我们想要的东西，这是值得的，目的将证明手段的正当性。

sentences.en: And that is why, when you get to the late 1990s, that is why the older Republicans often feel so betrayed by the Good Friday Agreement and the deal that the IRA ended up taking.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，当你进入20世纪90年代末时，年长的共和党人常常对《耶稣受难日协议》以及爱尔兰共和军最终接受的交易感到如此强烈的背叛感。

sentences.en: And by the older Republicans, you mean people who are from a generation before?
sentences.zh: 你所说的年长的共和党人，是指上一代人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but also people who've been in there since the 70s.
sentences.zh: 是的，但也包括那些自70年代起就加入其中人。

sentences.en: If you joined in 1970, right, and you're 20 years old, you are, what, getting into your 50s, maybe, by the time it all comes to an end?
sentences.zh: 如果你在1970年加入，没错，当时你20岁，那么等这一切结束的时候，你大概已经，什么，五十多岁了吧？

sentences.en: And the best part of your life, you know, your prime years are behind you.
sentences.zh: 而你人生中最美好的时光，你知道的，你人生的黄金岁月已经一去不复返了。

sentences.en: And you've spent those prime years doing things that you know are terrible things.
sentences.zh: 你把那些黄金岁月都用来做那些你知道极其可怕的事情。

sentences.en: You have killed innocent people, but you did it because you believed the end justified the means and the end was a united Ireland.

sentences.en: And now, your leaders tell you, actually, you did it so that you could get into coalition with Ian Paisley and run the waterboard.

sentences.en: And you say, what?
sentences.zh: 而你会说，什么？

sentences.en: I mean, we waded through blood.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们曾涉足血海。

sentences.en: We descended into hell.
sentences.zh: 我们曾坠入地狱。

sentences.en: We basically, you know, sold our immortal souls for this.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上，你知道的，为此出卖了不朽的灵魂。

sentences.en: And that's why people feel so aggrieved when Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness do the deal.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当杰里·亚当斯和马丁·麦吉尼斯达成这笔交易时，人们会感到如此愤慨。

sentences.en: I mean, you mentioned hell in Immortal Souls.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提到了地狱和不朽的灵魂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In that.
sentences.zh: 在那个问题上。
